questions.prompt: Explain what beginBackgroundTask does and why you must always call endBackgroundTask in 2 to 5 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Explains that beginBackgroundTask grants roughly 30 seconds to finish in-flight work before app suspension
Explains that failing to call endBackgroundTask triggers a watchdog timeout crash by the system

questions.modelAnswer: In UIKit, beginBackgroundTask asks iOS for extra execution time, typically around thirty seconds, to finish an in-flight operation when the app enters the background. Developers must always call endBackgroundTask once the work finishes or when the expiration handler fires. If you fail to end the task, the iOS watchdog timer kills the app process with an exception code.

questions.prompt: Explain the differences between BGAppRefreshTask and BGProcessingTask in 2 to 5 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Explains that BGAppRefreshTask is short (~30s) for updating feeds and current content
Explains that BGProcessingTask is longer (minutes) for heavy work and can require power and network

questions.modelAnswer: BGAppRefreshTask is designed for brief content updates, granting roughly thirty seconds to fetch fresh social feeds or weather data. In contrast, BGProcessingTask is intended for longer operations that take several minutes, such as database cleanup or machine learning indexing. BGProcessingTask also allows developers to specify that tasks only run when the device has external power and network connectivity.

questions.prompt: Explain why task identifiers must be registered in Info.plist and handlers registered at launch in 2 to 5 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Explains that Info.plist tells iOS which background tasks the app is permitted to run
Explains that registering handlers early in launch ensures the system can deliver wakeups properly

questions.modelAnswer: All background task identifiers must be declared in Info.plist under BGTaskSchedulerPermittedIdentifiers so iOS knows the app is authorized to schedule them. Submitting an unregistered identifier throws a runtime error. Furthermore, handlers must be registered before didFinishLaunchingWithOptions completes so the system can wake the app and invoke the matching handler immediately when conditions are met.

questions.prompt: Explain the role of task.expirationHandler on a BGTask and why it is critical in 2 to 5 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Explains that expirationHandler is called by iOS when allocated background time has expired
Explains using it to cancel ongoing async work cleanly and save state before termination

questions.modelAnswer: The expirationHandler is a closure invoked by iOS when the system decides that allocated background time has run out. It gives your app a brief opportunity to cancel ongoing asynchronous tasks, stop network connections, and save progress safely. If you do not handle expiration cleanly, the system terminates the process and reduces future background scheduling opportunities for your app.

questions.prompt: Explain how a senior iOS engineer handles large file downloads reliably in the background in 2 to 5 sentences.
questions.lessonSection: How to answer in the interview

rubric.criterion: Discusses using URLSessionConfiguration.background to delegate transfers to the system daemon nsurlsessiond
Explains that transfers continue even if the app process terminates or is suspended

questions.modelAnswer: A senior engineer relies on URLSessionConfiguration.background rather than attempting to keep the app process awake. This configuration delegates file downloads to the out-of-process system daemon nsurlsessiond, allowing transfers to continue even if the app process is suspended or terminated. Once downloads finish, the system wakes the app in the background and invokes handleEventsForBackgroundURLSession to process files.
